fdroid:app.pwhs.universalinstaller.name: Universal Installer

Universal Installer is a modern Android package manager and Split APK Installer built to sideload split APKs, bundled archives with OBB data, and install silently with Material 3 UI.
Expressive & Customizable

- Theme: High-contrast Orange theme by default with dynamic color support.
- Installer Profiles: Save and reuse install flags, spoofed installers, and target users.
Supported Formats
- APK, APK+, APKS, XAPK, and APKM split bundles.
- Zip archives containing Android packages.
Install From Anywhere
- Local file picker: Auto-scan storage, browse packages, or full filesystem browser.
- Remote download: Paste a direct URL to download and install packages.
- App integration: Open APKs from browsers, file managers, and messaging apps.
Preview Before Installing
- Inspect app name, icon, version, package ID, file size, target SDK, CPU architectures, permissions, and split/OBB details before installing.
OBB Support
- Automatic extraction and copying of bundled OBB files in XAPK/APKM.
- Manual Attachment: Attach standalone .obb files via the preview sheet.
- Background worker with persistent copy notifications.
Silent Installs: Shizuku, Root & Dhizuku
- Shizuku: Silent installs via wireless debugging without root.
- Root: Silent installs with advanced flags on rooted devices.
- Dhizuku: Device Owner installation without root or ADB.
- Targeted User Installs: Install to Work profile, cloned spaces, or all users.
- Custom installer spoofing and downgrade flags.
App Manager & Extractor
- Detailed list with APK size, install date, and usage stats.
- APK Backup: Extract and export installed apps to local storage.
- Batch operations: Multi-select for batch uninstall.
Sync & Share (LAN File Server)
- Built-in HTTP server: Share packages across local Wi-Fi.
- Web Dashboard: Transfer APKs between PC and phone without cables.
- PIN protection for local file transfer sessions.
Security & Privacy
- VirusTotal integration: Hash lookup and scan reports with your free API key.
- Offline-first: No internet required for core operations.
- 100% open source: No ads, no account requirement, and privacy respecting.
Device Utilities
- Storage overview and comprehensive install history logs.
- Multi-language support for 15+ languages.

fdroid:com.hazelhope.dubster.nightblast.description:
With Nightblast, you can send urgent alerts to your contacts using encrypted SMS messages, with vibrations and optional sounds.
 How it works: 
When you connect with another Nightblast user, your phones exchange encryption keys. After you've exchanged keys, you can send encrypted alerts to each other.
Just select contacts in the Recipients section, choose Just vibrations or Sounds and vibrations and write your message. Then tap the send icon.
Nightblast encrypts your message and sends it to the selected recipients over SMS. When Nightblast receives the alert on the recipient's phone, it displays an alert dialog and vibrates the device.
If you selected Sounds and vibrations , Nightblast will play a loud sound using the Alarms audio channel, using whatever volume your phone is set to for alarms, and, if your phone is configured to let alarms break through do not disturb, you'll hear it even if do not disturb is enabled.
 Disclaimer: 
Nightblast uses SMS messages to communicate between devices. If your carrier charges for SMS messages, using Nightblast may incur additional charges or use your texting quota.
Connecting with another contact uses up to 12 SMS messages , and sending an alert can use up to 6 SMS messages .

fdroid:com.tananaev.logcat.name: Logcat
fdroid:com.tananaev.logcat.description:
Read Android logs without root access. The app uses remote debugging to connect
to phone local ADB daemon. Configuring remote debugging on a phone can be
challenging and requires some technical expertise. It has to be done once and
after each device reboot.
Enable USB debugging first on your device. Navigate to Settings > About Phone
and tap Build number seven times. Go back, access the Developer options menu and
check USB debugging option.
Next step is to enable remote debugging. You need to have Android SDK installed
on your computer. Connect your phone via USB cable and run following adb
command:
adb tcpip 5555
Disconnect USB cable before trying to use the app. Some phones have problems
handling network ADB connection when they are connected via USB as well.
Sometimes establishing connection to ADB hangs and requires killing and
restarting the app. It seems to be a problem with ADB daemon itself and not the
app issue.

fdroid:io.github.ketandholakia.virc.name: VIRC
fdroid:io.github.ketandholakia.virc.summary: Multi-server IRC client: SASL, bouncers, IRCv3, notifications
fdroid:io.github.ketandholakia.virc.description:
VIRC (Vittix IRC Chat Client) is a modern, feature-rich multi-server IRC client for Android.
Features:
* Multi-server: stay connected to several IRC networks (Libera Chat, OFTC, and any other) at once
* Clean shell-and-drawer interface for switching quickly between channels and private messages
* Bouncer support (ZNC, soju) and SASL authentication (SCRAM-SHA-256, PLAIN fallback)
* IRCv3 support: server-time timestamps, chathistory gap backfill on join/reconnect, typing indicators
* Secure connections: TLS with trust-on-first-use certificate pinning for self-signed servers, plus STS policy enforcement
* Passwords stored in the device keychain; profile backups are AES-encrypted and password-protected
* Background keep-alive service keeps sessions connected while the app is in the background
* Smart reconnects with exponential backoff and flap detection
* Local notifications for private messages and mentions, with deep links straight into the channel
* Message history saved locally (SQLite) with pagination
* Slash commands: /join, /part, /msg, /query, /nick, /me, /topic, /identify, /whois, moderation commands and more
* Nickname and command auto-complete
VIRC is free and open source software. There are no ads, no analytics and no tracking - your messages go directly to the IRC server you choose.
Network notes: image previews for links posted in channels are fetched directly from your device and can be disabled in Settings. File uploads are sent only to the upload host you configure - a default is preset, and imgur, catbox and litterbox presets are included.

fdroid:io.github.munzzyy.sweep.name: Sweep
fdroid:io.github.munzzyy.sweep.summary: Plain-language stalkerware checkup. On-device, nothing stored or sent
fdroid:io.github.munzzyy.sweep.description:
"Is something on my phone watching me" is a normal question with a hard
answer. Sweep checks the places surveillance software actually lives:
* Installed apps against a public, maintained stalkerware list (Echap's
 indicators, bundled, matched by package name and signing certificate so
 renamed copies still match).
* Device admin apps and the powers they declare, such as locking or
 wiping the phone.
* Accessibility services that are turned on, and what Android says each
 one can do, like reading the screen or seeing what you type.
* Apps with notification access.
* Which sensitive permissions each app holds right now: microphone,
 camera, location, text messages, call history, contacts and more.
* Apps that start at boot or declare background services for location,
 the camera or the microphone.
* Keyboards, certificate authorities a person added, VPN apps and the
 always-on VPN setting.
* The default text message app, dialer and assistant, device and profile
 owners, and whether a work profile exists.
* USB and wireless debugging, developer options, and battery optimization
 exemptions.
* Apps with no launcher icon, and apps installed from outside any store,
 with when they arrived and what installed them.
* The screen lock, the last security update, signs of root, and on
 Android 16 whether Advanced Protection is on.
* If you turn on usage access for Sweep (it is off unless you do): how
 much data each flagged, hidden or sideloaded app sent in the last 30
 days and when it was last in use. A sign to weigh, never proof.
Every result opens with how many of these Sweep could actually read, and
lists what it could not read and why. Each finding is explained in
words. Sweep never says "you are safe": it says "these specific checks
found nothing", and means exactly that. Matches lead with
do-not-confront guidance and advocate hotlines, because removing
stalkerware can escalate a dangerous situation.
One permission it needs (listing installed apps, which is the checkup
itself), usage access only if you switch it on, a yes or no read of
Advanced Protection, and no internet permission, so what Sweep sees
cannot leave your phone.
Results are never stored. A Leave fast button sits on every screen.
Runs on Android 9 and newer, with Android System WebView 87 or newer.
Android 9 has had no security fixes since January 2022, so on a phone that
old the checkup tells you less: spyware that got in through an unpatched
hole might not show up as an app.
Beta: offered to domain organizations for review. Treat Sweep as one
tool, not an authority.

fdroid:org.opendataensemble.formulus.name: Formulus
fdroid:org.opendataensemble.formulus.summary: Offline-first bespoke data collection apps from Open Data Ensemble
fdroid:org.opendataensemble.formulus.description:
Formulus is the mobile data collection client of the Open Data Ensemble (ODE) platform.
It allows organizations, research teams, and public sector institutions to build their own bespoke data collection applications based on structured forms defined using the JSONForms specification.
Forms and application logic are defined externally, meaning the same Formulus app can host many different data collection projects without requiring app updates.
Key features include:
• Flexible form-based data collection using JSONForms
• Offline-first operation for use in the field
• Secure bi-directional synchronization with an ODE Synkronus server
• Support for complex data structures and validation
• Designed for long-term maintainability and open standards
Formulus is particularly suited for environments where reliable data collection is needed under challenging conditions, such as:
• field research
• public health surveillance
• environmental monitoring
• humanitarian and development projects
• decentralized data collection initiatives
The app requires access to an ODE Synkronus server for synchronization and project management. Organizations typically run their own Synkronus server to host forms, manage users, and collect submitted data.
If you do not yet have access to a Synkronus server but would like to explore the application, a public demonstration environment may be available. See the project website for details.
Formulus is part of the Open Data Ensemble ecosystem, an open-source initiative focused on building interoperable tools for decentralized, standards-based data collection.
Source code and documentation:
https://opendataensemble.org

fdroid:pro.kwiatek.tune_tangler.name: Tune Tangler
fdroid:pro.kwiatek.tune_tangler.summary: Enjoy your music — record, refine, remix, share.
fdroid:pro.kwiatek.tune_tangler.description:
Tune Tangler is a simple grid for short musical ideas. Record with the built-in microphone or USB-connected audio hardware. You can also load a file from the device.
Play tracks together so they stay in time, or run them independently. Use looping or a single pass — whatever you need. All recordings and
settings are kept after you close the app. You can share tracks or save the whole project as a ZIP file.
NAVIGATION
The top bar shows the app title: the logo on the left opens the side menu; on the right, start/stop all tracks and a “⋮” menu for actions
for the whole grid at once — ZIP project export/import, shared playback tweaks, trim resets, and More settings… (which also opens the side menu).
The side menu lists Help, Recording, Tracks & Grid (including keyboard shortcut presets), Screen, Permissions, the maintenance area, and
profiles at the bottom.
WORKING THE GRID
Each colored block is a quick control: tap it, or — with a keyboard connected — press the matching shortcut key. Want sliders and finer
options? Hold the block — or, with an external keyboard connected, press your shortcut key together with Ctrl. Set each track’s shortcut in its
details.
Each grid row also has start/stop for that row and a “⋮” menu with bulk actions for every track in that row (playback mode, level,
balance, speed, trim resets, delete that row’s recordings).
In the side menu, pick a preset shortcut map for your keyboard: standard (PC-style, flexible grid) or the 24-key 6×4 layout.
INSIDE A TRACK
Trim the start and end, choose loop or single pass, set level and left/right balance, change playback speed, name the track, and assign a
shortcut. Move the track on the grid, replace the audio with another file, share a recording, or clear the slot.
ICONS ON THE BLOCK
Icons show shortcuts, audio source, level, balance, trim, and loop mode. Open Help from the side menu for a full legend.
RECORDING QUALITY
Settings include file format, time resolution, bit rate (bitrate), mono or stereo, and — when the device supports it — automatic level
control (AGC), less room echo, and quieter background noise.
SETTINGS PROFILES
Profiles store full setups: recording options plus language, light or dark theme, accent color, and keeping the screen on. Save several
profiles, switch with a tap, remove one with a long press.
PROJECT ZIP EXPORT
One ZIP file holds the grid layout, every track’s settings, and the audio, with a short integrity check and a small summary (version,
export time, grid size, and recording statistics). Import shows a preview and a warning before overwriting. The app rejects damaged or incomplete files.
PERMISSIONS
Microphone (and USB audio when the OS allows), storage for imports and exports, and optional Android notifications if you record while the
app is in the background.
For a fuller guide to the icons and options, open Help in the side menu.

apple-macos:1560781471.description:

Record locations as tracks and waypoints. Create and update custom layers and attributes. Style (symbology) of vector layers is highly customisable.
Bit Map was the first iOS app to provide navigation with arbitrary user-supplied maps in 2009.

apple-macos:1534513553.name: Health Notes - Fresh Start
apple-macos:1534513553.description:
Health Notes is a personal health archive for people who want to keep blood pressure, blood sugar, weight, heart rate, temperature, meds, and checkup notes in one place over time. It helps you turn scattered daily numbers, follow-up visits, and recovery notes into a record you can revisit later.The app grew out of the developer's own long-term health tracking needs while living with chronic illness. That perspective shaped the product around consistency, clarity, and keeping data in a form that you and your family can actually understand months later.
You decide what each note should track. A blood pressure note can hold systolic, diastolic, and pulse together. A glucose note can combine fasting values, post-meal values, and meds from the same day. A symptom note can mix temperature, status options, and free text. If Apple's Health app does not already offer the exact structure you need, you can build your own.
Over time, those notes become a cleaner personal history of what changed, when it changed, and how your body felt along the way.
Your data stays on your devices and in iCloud, so it can sync across iPhone, iPad, and Mac. When needed, you can export to CSV or Excel for your own backup, family sharing, or conversations with a clinician.
You can also import selected historical data from the Health app to give a note a starting point, or copy the template structure of an existing Note to create a new one for yourself or a family member. Health app import is currently available on iPhone only, works as a one-time historical import, and does not include document-style lab reports.
Health Notes focuses on one job: helping you organize and keep long-term health data. It is built for personal records, family care, and day-to-day health context over time.

An interface to Digital Audio Players implementing Media Transfer Protocol
 with a focus on MTP features such as full metadata support, albums,
 and playlists.
 This is especially useful for MP3 players that rely on the host computer
 to provide metadata for the device to display the information, such as
 artist or the track name.
 Note that while Android devices use MTP, they do not use the metadata
 functionality. The packages bundled with the operating system are
 sufficient for browsing the files on Android.
 Known issues:
 1. UI still hangs during some MTP operations; the system will show a
 warning dialog about application not responding, but the app is working.

 will be unable to connect.
 You can also disable GNOME automount with the following commands:
 gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.media-handling automount false
 gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.media-handling automount-open false

 while it is running due to device caching in the underlying libusb
 library.

flathub:org.denemo.Denemo.name: Denemo
flathub:org.denemo.Denemo.description:
Denemo is a music notation program that lets you rapidly enter notation. Music can be typed in at the PC-Keyboard, or played in via MIDI controller. The typesetting is done in the background by LilyPond while you work, and is generally flawless publication quality. Any final tweaks to can be done on the final typeset score with the mouse if needed. This represents an enormous practical improvement over the most programs which require you to re-position colliding notation constantly as you enter the music.
 Unique to Denemo are methods to enter music in a musical, rather than mechanical, manner. You play in a phrase or two of the music using the number keys to indicate the note durations. Audible feedback lets you hear what you have entered; playing the phrase a second time on a real instrument adds the pitches to the rhythm. Again, Denemo gives you audible feedback so that you don’t enter E-flat when you meant D-sharp etc.
 Another great feature is the ability to put links in the score to the original source document that you transcribed from. Clicking on such a link opens the document for you and highlights the bar you are looking at. You can use this to continue work from where you left off, or for looking back at the source to check a doubtful bar.

firefox-addons:3022240.name: Kick Chat Translator: Live Chat Translation
firefox-addons:3022240.summary: Free live chat translator for Kick: every message is translated into your language as it arrives, and your replies go out in the channel's language. No account, no setup. Works on live streams and VODs.
firefox-addons:3022240.description:
Kick Chat Translator is a free live chat translator for Kick. Read any stream's chat in your own language, and reply in the channel's language, right inside the chat.
Watching a Turkish, Spanish, Russian or Arabic stream and can't follow the chat? Install, open the stream, and every message shows its translation right under it as it arrives. No account, no API key, nothing to set up.
HOW IT WORKS
 Open any Kick stream. A green bar at the top of the chat shows the translator is on.
 Each new message gets its translation underneath, in your browser's language.
 Type a reply in your own language. A preview shows it in the channel's language: press Tab or click it, then send.
The channel's language is read from Kick itself, and both languages can be changed in settings. Works on live streams and on VOD replays, keeps 7TV emotes as they are, and pauses itself in background tabs.
See it running on a real chat: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NoGJeUrwy9o 
WHAT YOU GET
• 43 languages, right to left included (Arabic, Hebrew, Persian), with regional variants kept apart (Brazilian Portuguese, Traditional Chinese).
• Free out of the box with Google Translate, no key and no account.
• Better European languages with your own DeepL API key. DeepL gets the recent chat lines as context, so the wording fits the conversation.
• Automatic fallback: when one engine fails, MyMemory or Lingva takes over. You choose the order.
• Four display styles: under the message, on the same line, in small italics after it, or only when you hover. Hover mode translates nothing until you point at a message, which cuts usage about ten times on a fast chat.
• Filters: skip bots, mute users or channels, hide lines that contain a word you choose (handy against !command spam), or translate only the languages you want.
• Emotes, mentions, links and emoji spam are stripped before anything is sent, so nothing is spent translating "kkkkkk".
• Make it yours: text size, line spacing, typeface, accent colour, dark or light chat, a reading language remembered per channel, keyboard shortcuts.
• Interface in the same 43 languages, right to left included, picked from a menu that shows each flag.
WHAT LEAVES YOUR BROWSER
Chat text goes only to the translation engine you picked. With Google, MyMemory or Lingva, that is the text of each message and nothing else: not the channel, not who said it. With DeepL, the last few chat lines go along as context, with the names of whoever wrote them, so the translation fits the conversation. That is what the "website content" line in the permissions above refers to, and it is the whole of it. There is no account and no server of mine: the extension talks to Kick and to the engine you chose, nothing else. If you tick the optional "technical and interaction data" choice, it also sends Google Analytics a daily anonymous count of engines used, errors and speed, never your messages, names or channels.
FREE AND OPEN SOURCE
MIT licence, every line of code public: github.com/Pkkls/kick-chat-translator 
Bug reports and language requests are welcome there.

apple-macos:6741387113.description:

- Market news headlines that give context to price movements
- Personal watchlists so you can follow the assets you care about
- A clean, TV-first interface designed for the big screen and remote navigation
Pro

The monthly plan includes a 7-day free trial for new subscribers; the annual plan has no trial. Subscriptions renew automatically until cancelled.
Where it runs
Apple TV, iPad, Mac and Apple Vision Pro.
Who it's for
People who want to watch the markets, not trade them. Analysts, market enthusiasts, newsrooms, offices and anyone who likes having live market information visible during the day.
Disclaimer
Market TV does not provide investment advice. Displayed prices are informational and may be delayed. Consult a licensed financial professional before making investment decisions.

fdroid:org.videomator.name: Videomator
fdroid:org.videomator.summary: Open-source multi-track video and audio editor
fdroid:org.videomator.description:
Videomator is a free and open-source multi-track video and audio editor for Android, in the style of Vegas Pro / CapCut.
Features:
- Multi-track timeline (video tracks with picture-in-picture overlays + audio tracks)
- Non-destructive editing: trim with finger handles, split, merge (real render), duplicate, ripple delete
- Real-time playback of the whole mix on a single clock (AudioTrack), with live edits during playback
- Clip effects: volume, pitch (semitones, duration preserved), speed, fade in/out, presets
- Video: rotate, flip, crop, brightness/contrast/saturation, overlay position/size/opacity
- Microphone recording directly into the timeline
- Timeline markers, A-B loop, metronome, snap to grid/clip edges/playhead
- Undo/redo, multi-select with contextual toolbar, range selection on the ruler
- Export: MP4 (H.264 + AAC) via the platform MediaCodec pipeline, or WAV / M4A audio mixdown
- Projects saved as portable JSON, with autosave
No accounts, no network, no proprietary code: video and audio are processed entirely with the platform codecs (MediaExtractor / MediaCodec / MediaMuxer / AudioTrack / AudioRecord). All dependencies are free software (AndroidX, Kotlin coroutines, Gson).
License: AGPL-3.0-only.
